title: Kernel signature regressor with prefetch + conservative-fallback for mixed-prefill/decode flows
creator: Lina Chen
description: Implement a lightweight online regressor that maps per-request signatures (architecture, seqlen, batch, kv-cache state, quantization profile, temperature) to a ranked kernel portfolio and confidence score. Use small microbench probes (<=2ms per probe) run in the warmup phase to correct model drift and kick off a prefetch warmstart for favored kernels. If confidence or probe results indicate instability, fall back to a conservative kernel (well-tested, latency-stable) and emit gating telemetry for post-mortem tuning.
motivation: Existing heuristic ensembles depend on static seqlen buckets and offline microbenchmarks which miss drift caused by mixed workloads, quantized variants, and hot switches between prefill and decode paths. This leads to tail latency spikes on multimodal customer traffic and conservative overprovisioning. A low-cost online regressor plus microprobe feedback can adapt to per-request conditions and safely improve p95 and unit cost while preserving SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Deployable regressor service integrated into runtime kernel picker with <1.5ms median decision latency
Microprobe harness that runs probes only during prefill warmup and adds <=2ms overhead on median requests
Safeguarded conservative fallback that prevents any p99 regression compared to baseline (current kernel selector) during 2-week canary
Automated telemetry: per-request chosen kernel, regressor confidence, probe latency, probe divergence flag, rollback events
A/B canary demonstrating >=8% reduction in p95 latency for mixed short/long seqlen workloads and >=5% token-cost reduction on 90th-percentile CPU/GPU utilization scenarios
design_notes: Architecture: lightweight regressor (XGBoost-like tree ensemble) served as a local inference lib inside the runtime process to avoid RPC overhead. Input features: hardware fingerprint (arch id, SMs, clock), CUDA driver version, model opset signature, effective seqlen, batch size, kv-cache hit-rate estimate, quantization level (int8/4bit/float16), recent latency rolling mean, temperature/runtime policy flags. Output: ranked list of candidate kernels with scores and a confidence scalar. Online microprobe: schedule 1-3 tiny microbenchmarks on prefills that exercise attention and matmul kernels; probes run on cold path only (first N tokens) and their results are fed back to the regressor's feature vector in-flight. Safety: when confidence < threshold OR probe divergence > delta, pick conservative kernel from the curated safe set and emit telemetry. Rollout: shadow mode -> 1% canary -> 10% canary -> wide rollout with automatic rollback on SLO triggers. Persist lightweight model updates to a versioned store and allow pinning per-customer.
implementation_plan: 1) Add feature extractor to runtime (ENG changes): gather runtime-only signals and normalize. 2) Implement local regressor artifact and small runtime API for selection. 3) Microprobe harness: inject probes at prefill warmup with strict CPU/GPU time budget. 4) Confidence gating + conservative fallback policy. 5) Telemetry: new metrics and logs for model decisions. 6) End-to-end testing on perfbench; 7) Canary rollout and monitoring. Timeline: 4 sprints (8 points).
experiment_results: Lab: mixed workload replay (60% short seqlen <= 64, 30% mid 128-512, 10% long >1024) on A100-40GB and T4 cluster. Baseline selector p95: 132ms (A100), 340ms (T4). With regressor+probe: p95: 116ms (-12%) on A100, 305ms (-10.3%) on T4. Median overhead added by probes: 1.2ms. Cost proxy (GPU-seconds per 1M tokens) reduced by ~7% on A100 scenarios with quantized int8 models. Notable regression: a small subset of long-batch prefills saw 3% p99 increase when probe budget set too high; fixed by tightening probe budget and stronger conservative fallback threshold. All experiments reproducible: perfbench run-id: rbw-2026-03-08-ksr-01.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: probes add jitter to latency-sensitive requests. Mitigation: run probes only on warmup tokens and rate-limit per-GPU; fall back to safe kernel if probe budget exceeded. Risk: model overfitting to stale hardware signatures. Mitigation: online lightweight drift detection and periodic retrain with curated dataset. Risk: supply chain for local model updates (security). Mitigation: sign models, require signed rollout, and integrate with KMS for model fetch authentication.
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: regressor.decision_latency_ms, regressor.confidence, kernel_probe.latency_ms, kernel_probe.divergence_flag, kernel_selector.fallback_count, kernel_selector.rollback_reason. Dashboard: runtime -> kernel-signature-regressor. Alerts: >0.5% of requests with fallback_count spike in 5m or p99 regression > baseline by 5% triggers pager.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: shadow-only (2 days) across controlled fleet. Phase 1: 1% live canary for non-critical tenants (48 hours). Phase 2: 10% canary with active SLO monitoring (72 hours). Phase 3: 100% with gradual ramp. Rollback criteria: sustained p99 > baseline (5m aggregated), fallback_count > 2% of requests, or probe overhead above configured budget.
